title: Weapons and Tactics Instructor-Air Officer (II/III) (LtCol to 2ndLt) and (CWO5 to WO) FMOS, DC AVN
raw_text:
30. MOS 8077, Weapons and Tactics Instructor-Air Officer (II/III) (LtCol to
2ndLt) and (CWO5 to WO) FMOS, DC AVN

    a. Summary. This MOS requires formal Air Officer instruction, training
and certification. It forms the foundation skill for assignment as Air
Officers and JTAC-I. A Weapons and Tactics Instructor – Air Officer directs
and controls close air support missions and advises commanders of ground
units on matters pertaining to air support. In addition, this individual is
responsible to the commander for directing and managing a units air support
training plan.

       b.   Prerequisites

            (1) Must hold MOS 7502 or 8002.

            (2) Security requirement:     secret security clearance eligible.

    c. Requirements. Must successfully complete the MAWTS-1 Air Officer
Course (M140E11), MCAS Yuma, AZ.

       d.   Duties

            (1) Manage a unit’s weapons and tactics training program.

        (2) Perform academic, simulation, and operational instruction on all
facets of aviation integration.

        (3) Serve as the ground commander’s primary advisor on aviation
integration.

        (4) Analyze performance and provide corrective guidance to members of
a unit’s tactical air control party.

        (5) Instruct on current enemy capabilities and the tactics to counter
their threat.

    e. Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code.
Teachers and Instructors, All Other 25-3099.

       f.   Related Military Skill.     None.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
